screening.reason: Meets inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE resting-state fMRI dynamic functional-connectivity variability for both a group-difference finding and ASD vs control classification.

evidence_spans.text:
We limited ourselves to
acquisitions with repetition time of 2s (sites NYU, SDSU, UM, USM). This
resulted in a dataset of 147 subjects with ASD and 146 healthy controls.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort restricted to four ABIDE sites with TR=2s: 147 ASD, 146 healthy controls.

evidence_spans.text:
The pre-processed acquisitions are
available as part of the Pre-processed Connectome Project (http://preprocessed- connectomes-project.org/abide/, C-PAC pipeline).
evidence_spans.claim: Data were preprocessed via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project, CPAC pipeline.

evidence_spans.text:
We
extracted rsfMRI time series using a 200-region parcellation CC200[?], estimated
subject-wise time-resolved connectivity matrices with windows lengths ranging
from 10 to 20 volumes (20-40s) and calculated node variability.
evidence_spans.claim: Dynamic functional connectivity was computed with sliding-window correlations over the CC200 atlas.

evidence_spans.text:
For inter-site, we employed a leave-
one-out-site approach that involved training the classiﬁer on all the sites
except the one left out for testing.
evidence_spans.claim: Inter-site evaluation used a leave-one-site-out approach.

evidence_spans.text:
Our analysis revealed that pa-
tients diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) show increased
FC variability in several brain regions that are associated with low FC
variability in the typical brain.
evidence_spans.claim: ASD patients showed increased dynamic FC variability in regions that are low-variability in typical controls.

evidence_spans.text:
We then used the enhanced FC variability
of brain regions as features for training machine learning models for ASD
classiﬁcation and achieved 65%
evidence_spans.claim: Node-variability features gave up to 65% classification accuracy.

evidence_spans.text:
Table 1 summarizes the performance of diﬀerent
classiﬁers on intra-site ASD prediction. The accuracy achieved by all classiﬁers
is comparable and is around 60%. The sensitivity varies between 60 to 65%. The
speciﬁcity is ˜60% for SVM and MLP, whereas RF and NB produce slightly lower
speciﬁcity.
evidence_spans.claim: Intra-site 5-fold CV: accuracy ~60%, sensitivity 60-65%, specificity ~60% (SVM, MLP).

evidence_spans.text:
The results on inter-site classiﬁcation are presented in Table 3. Whereas
the classiﬁcation accuracy using MLP is ˜62% for all sites, the speciﬁcity and
sensitivity vary across sites, consistent with the results shown in Figure 1b.
evidence_spans.claim: Leave-one-site-out classification accuracy using MLP was ~62% across sites.

assessments.support: N by diagnosis and site restriction (TR=2s sites only) are given, but no motion/QC exclusion rule beyond the TR filter is reported: "We limited ourselves to acquisitions with repetition time of 2s (sites NYU, SDSU, UM, USM). This resulted in a dataset of 147 subjects with ASD and 146 healthy controls."
CPAC pipeline and CC200 atlas with sliding-window dynamic connectivity clearly described.
ASD/control labels are the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis, independent of the connectivity-derived predictors.

Both intra-site 5-fold cross-validation (pooled across sites) and a leave-one-site-out inter-site evaluation are reported; the intra-site pooled scenario does not control for site, but the leave-one-site-out scenario does, and no leakage-control statement is given for the node-selection step based on "a positive group-level diﬀerence across the three big sites (NYU, UM, and USM)" used to pick features.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort and pipeline/atlas are reasonably well described; the study reports both a pooled intra-site 5-fold CV (no site control) and a leave-one-site-out inter-site evaluation (site controlled), with a possible leakage route where a feature subset is chosen using group differences across the same sites used later for training/testing.

charting.specific_features: Sliding-window dynamic functional connectivity (node variability) and static node strength, using the CC200 atlas
charting.specific_algorithms: Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Multilayer Perceptron
charting.validation_methodology: Intra-site 5-fold cross-validation (pooled and site-balanced variants) and inter-site leave-one-site-out cross-validation
charting.key_performance_results: Up to 65% accuracy using node-variability features; intra-site 5-fold CV ~60% accuracy, 60-65% sensitivity, ~60% specificity (SVM, MLP); inter-site leave-one-site-out MLP accuracy ~62%
charting.features_associated_disorder: Brain regions with low FC variability in typical controls show increased FC variability in ASD
charting.feature_change_direction: Increased (hyper-variability) dynamic functional connectivity in ASD relative to controls
charting.dataset_openly_available: No code repository or participant-list availability statement found; data referenced via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project public resource

items.support: N by diagnosis and site restriction given, no further exclusion rule.
CPAC pipeline named via Preprocessed Connectomes Project, no version/strategy detail.
ASD/control labels are the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis; this paper does not restate diagnostic criteria.
Node-subset selection used group differences across the same evaluation sites with no stated train/test separation.
Leave-one-site-out inter-site evaluation reported alongside the pooled intra-site variant.
No code or participant-list availability statement.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Both (group-difference + diagnostic prediction); ABIDE, four TR=2s sites (NYU, SDSU, UM, USM), 147 ASD and 146 healthy controls.
narrative_row.methods: CPAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; CC200 atlas sliding-window dynamic functional connectivity (node variability) and static node strength; SVM/RF/NB/MLP classifiers with intra-site 5-fold CV and inter-site leave-one-site-out evaluation.
narrative_row.outcomes: ASD showed increased FC variability in regions of otherwise-low variability in controls; classification reached up to 65% accuracy (intra-site) and ~62% accuracy (inter-site leave-one-site-out, MLP).
narrative_row.key_limitations: No motion/QC threshold beyond a TR restriction; possible feature-selection leakage from choosing nodes by cross-site group differences; no code or participant-list availability.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: An early dynamic-FC approach to ABIDE combining a group-difference finding with both pooled and leave-one-site-out classification evaluation.

kg_link.cohort_description: ABIDE acquisitions restricted to repetition time 2s at four sites (NYU, SDSU, UM, USM): 147 ASD, 146 healthy controls.
kg_link.finding: ASD patients show increased dynamic FC variability in regions of low variability in typical controls; node-variability-based classifiers reached up to 65% accuracy (intra-site) and ~62% accuracy (inter-site leave-one-site-out, MLP).
